chunks: The first of them: He whom Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Askari and Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad, his son, appointed (them, peace be upon them),
He is the trusted elder, Abu Amr Uthman ibn Saeed al-Amari, may Allah have mercy on him. He belonged to the Asadi tribe, but he was named al-Amari:
ai.seo_question: Who was the first emissary appointed by the Imams during the occultation?
ai.summary: This passage establishes Uthman ibn Saeed al-Amari as the inaugural *na'ib al-khas* (special deputy) of the Twelfth Imam, appointed directly by Imam al--Hasan al-Askari and his father Imam Ali al-Hadi, marking the beginning of the Minor Occultation. The text clarifies his tribal affiliation with the Asadiyya while noting his distinct nisba, al-Amari, which likely derives from his residence in the Amariyya district of Samarra, a detail significant for identifying him in early Shia biographical dictionaries. His designation as 'trusted' (*al-mu'tamad*) underscores the foundational authority of the deputyship system that bridged the gap between the Imam and the general community.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: Abu Amr Uthman bin Saeed Amari, He was the first emissary during the period of occultation, who was appointed to this position by Imam Hadi and Imam Hasan Askari (a.s).
He was a trusted elder of the society. His name was Abu Amr Uthman bin Saeed Amari, may Allah have mercy on him. He belonged to the Asadi tribe, but was named as Amari.
